answer: A proof-of-capacity protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to commit cryptographic plot tables to persistent storage. An attacker creating fake identities incurs the verifiable capital cost of provisioning physical ferrous disks for challenge responses. While network queries drift like a zephyr, nodes must prove sector retention to join the ivory admission registry. A key limitation is that large datacenters with idle storage can still amass disproportionate influence.
